sec: Type-II AIH features and treatment algorithm

items.q: Type-II AIH — judge: I Seen in children. II Carries a good prognosis. III Associated with HLA DR-7.
opts: I and III true, II false
I true, II and III false
II and III true, I false
items.exp: 'Seen in children; Poor prognosis; A/w HLA DR-7'. (Book p1025)

items.q: Disease associations of Type-II AIH — which is NOT printed?
items.exp: 'Disease Association : Diabetes mellitus Type-1, Vitiligo, Autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome Type-1.' RA is the HLA-DR04 Type-1 association (p1023). (Book p1025)

items.q: Treatment flowchart: once AIH is diagnosed, what is checked for by Fibroscan before treatment?
items.exp: 'Diagnosed AIH — Fibroscan, check for → Cirrhosis'. (Book p1025)

items.q: What is the printed steroid regimen for AIH and the taper duration?
opts: 1 mg/kg/day × 4 weeks, then taper over 12 weeks
items.exp: 'Steroid 1 mg/kg/day × 4 weeks → Taper → 12 weeks' +/− Azathioprine. (1 mg/kg × 7 days over 3 weeks is the alcoholic-hepatitis regimen, p1028.) (Book p1025)

items.q: Fill up: Steroid in AIH is given '+/− ______', and response is assessed 'After ______ months'.
items.exp: '+/− Azathioprine' and 'After 3–4 months' the outcome branches to remission or relapse. (Book p1025)

items.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the four printed criteria of remission?
opts: ↓ S. bilirubin and liver enzymes back to normal
items.exp: Remission: Symptomatic improvement; Histological improvement; ↓ S. bilirubin; Liver enzyme back to normal. (Book p1025)

items.q: A patient relapses after 3–4 months of steroid ± azathioprine. What does the flowchart direct, and what caveat follows?
